chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Running the band after Danny left; Kentucky State lecturers and campus life
summary: Jones led the Collegians after Danny left and recalls campus visitors Mary McLeod Bethune, Robert Weaver and Dr. DuBois.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, let me see. I guess I wound up doing most of it. But we kind of split the responsibility around, you know, passed it around.

And we kept it going. Because I wanted to stay in school and try to put something in my head. Because a lot of the guys came back home to Chicago, went back home, rather, and then a lot of us stayed. Those that wanted to stay stayed and those that wanted to go back home, they went home, you know?
And I've never regretted it. Never regretted one minute of it, because it made me grow as a person. And made me much more well rounded person.
Yeah, I'm sure it was a fine experience.

Yes, it was good. The campus life and meeting different people and had a chance to meet so many people. We had one building where every week there would be a lecturer that would come there and lecture, and I had a chance to meet Mrs. Bethune, because she did some of the baccalaureate services there.
Yeah, that's right. And, oh, Robert Weaver, who became a big man in Washington later.

And Dr. DuBois. And then there was another very prominent from Howard University. Gee, I can't think of his name. It was Stuart -- I just can't think of his last name. But he was a great jazz historian. They had textbooks on jazz way back then.
Yes. He was an English teacher at Howard.
Stuart -- Ellington knew him, knew him very well. Gee whiz, but I can't think of his name now.
Well, if you think of it later let's drop it in.
